chunks: And through this chain, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Nisaburi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The master of this matter must have seclusion, and in his seclusion there must be strength, and he is not lonely among thirty, and how good an abode is Tayba.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Matter (referring to Imam al-Mahdi)
key_terms.طَيْبَةٌ: Tayba (a name for Medina or a state of goodness)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the Imam's seclusion during the occultation according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the spiritual and physical conditions of the Mahdi's occultation, asserting that his seclusion is characterized by divine strength and companionship rather than isolation. The mention of 'thirty' refers to a select group of companions who provide him with comfort, while 'Tayba' alludes to Medina or a state of spiritual purity, reinforcing the concept of protected seclusion (ghayba) in Shia eschatology.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 121 - Through the same chains, it is narrated from Fadhl bin Shazan Nishaburi from Abdur Rahman bin Abi Najran from Ali bin Abi Hamza from Abu Basir from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) that he said: “
The man of this matter must disappear and he is to be in isolation during his disappearance. There is in no loneliness among the thirty and how good an abode ‘Tayba’ is!”
